A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SoFlow research. All 19 pages of each version, including equations, figures, tables, and appendices, support comparison. v2 retains Appendices A–E and adds Appendix F.

before.justification: v1 reports original ImageNet and CIFAR-10 generation results, hyperparameter ablations, model-scaling results, and training-efficiency measurements in Tables 1–3 and 5 and Figure 3.

after.justification: v2 retains these original experimental results, including the benchmark comparisons and efficiency measurements, with two updated ablation scores in Table 1.

M1.justification: Sections 4.1–4.3 and Algorithm 1 retain the same solution-function parameterizations, Flow Matching and consistency losses, CFG velocity mixing, and sampling procedures. The correction from x to x_t in the network description is not a method change.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate class-conditional ImageNet 256×256 generation in VAE latent space and unconditional CIFAR-10 32×32 generation in pixel space. No dataset, task, or test scenario is added or removed.

E2.justification: Comparator membership is unchanged in the ImageNet comparison in Table 2, the CIFAR-10 comparison in Table 3, and the MeanFlow/SoFlow efficiency comparison in Appendix D.

E3.justification: Both retain FID evaluation on 50,000 generated samples, the same sampling budgets, DiT-B/4 ablations trained for 400K iterations, and the main ImageNet models trained for 240 epochs. Appendix A and Table 4 retain the experimental settings; no protocol change accompanies the updated scores.

E4.justification: Table 1a and 1c revise the quantitative evidence for sensitivity to the intermediate-time schedule and loss-weighting exponent. All six ablation designs and their interpretations remain intact, as do the model-scaling and efficiency analyses.

E5.justification: Results remain point estimates. Neither version adds repeated-run counts, seed information, confidence intervals, error bars, or significance tests.

E6.justification: Table 1a changes the cosine-schedule FID from 61.93 to 60.17, and Table 1c changes the p=0.5 FID from 60.37 to 59.04 under unchanged reported settings. Rankings remain unchanged, and other numerical results and visual samples are retained. The PDFs do not explain the reason for these updates.

T1.justification: The main-text mathematical formulation and Appendix E retain the same assumptions, derivations, lemma, proofs, and solution/ODE-error bounds. Differences in mathematical typography and equivalent notation do not alter the theory.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and conclusion retain the same claims: one-step generation trained from scratch, CFG support without JVP computation, and better ImageNet FID than MeanFlow under matched architectures and training epochs.

C2.justification: The interpretations of schedule sensitivity, loss weighting, CFG, velocity mixing, and model scaling are unchanged. Appendix D retains the qualification that efficiency depends on implementation, hardware, and framework support.

D1.justification: Appendices A, C, and D retain the same hardware, optimizers, hyperparameters, augmentation details, pseudocode, and efficiency-comparison implementation. The code link and VAE access reference are unchanged.

R1.justification: The cited works and related-work positioning are unchanged. Adding 'Technical Report' to the Krizhevsky et al. reference is a bibliographic metadata update.

P1.justification: v2 adds Appendix F stating that large language models were used only to polish writing. Other edits are limited notation, wording, cross-reference, and bibliographic refinements; the existing narrative and section order remain substantially unchanged.

P2.justification: v2 adopts the ICLR conference layout throughout, changing margins, typography, running headers, heading and caption styles, figure/table sizes, and text placement. Figures 1–5 retain their visual content, but the document-wide presentation is substantially reformatted.

improvement.justification: The two Table 1 updates preserve the ablation rankings and interpretations, while the principal benchmark results, proofs, and reproducibility information remain unchanged. The conference reformatting and brief writing-assistance disclosure do not materially change the paper's evidential strength, completeness, or clarity.
